key_insight: Structured, permissioned access to application state can turn an LLM chat interface into a workspace-wide control layer while preserving user control.
engineering_relevance: AI-enabled applications should expose state and capabilities through permissioned interfaces, with a separate control-plane boundary for agents that can modify their own settings.
method: Define a capability ladder from feature tutoring and settings access to retrieval, confirmed changes, and full orchestration.
Build bounded context from summaries, settings, and relevant messages in the Meta Chat prototype.
Link workspace references and support confirmed, reversible changes, browsable tutorials, and user-started persona conversations.
evidence_signal: The abstract grounds the proposal in the Meta Chat prototype for Chat AI but reports no quantitative evaluation or comparative results.
watch_item: Workspace access introduces privacy, grounding, and prompt-injection risks, requiring explicit permissions and protected control boundaries.
paper_title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
